title: 彭博社统计：Alphabet、Meta、微软、亚马逊、甲骨文承诺投入超3万亿美元建AI基础设施
content:
彭博社统计：Alphabet、Meta、微软、亚马逊、甲骨文承诺投入超3万亿美元建AI基础设施
AI 基建掀起军备竞赛：微软、谷歌、甲骨文等巨头承诺投入超 3 万亿美元
据彭博社10月31日报道，Alphabet、Meta、微软、亚马逊和甲骨文五大巨头承诺未来数年在数据中心等领域投入超过3万亿美元（约20.01万亿元人民币）。其中谷歌支出承诺超1万亿美元、接近一年前的八倍，Meta超8,000亿美元且近半用于最长分30年支付的租约；甲骨文是首家因投资AI数据中心而自由现金流转负的大型科技公司，预计到2028年恢复正自由现金流。
原文汇总五巨头财报披露的支出承诺构成和自由现金流变化，读者可以据此看清各家AI基建投入的规模差异与回收压力。
IT之家 10 月 31 日消息，据彭博社今天（31 日）凌晨报道，AI 基础设施建设仍将吸引巨额资金。Alphabet、Meta、微软、亚马逊和甲骨文五大科技巨头承诺，未来数年将在数据中心等领域投入超过 3 万亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 20.01 万亿元人民币）。
随着数据中心建设竞赛愈演愈烈，五家公司披露的租赁、建筑、能源及设备采购承诺大幅增长。这些资金有的将在短期内支出，有的则涉及未来数十年的长期合同。
谷歌的支出承诺规模最大。根据 Alphabet 提交的监管文件，包括技术设备、能源和租赁在内的合同承诺总额超过 1 万亿美元（现汇率约合 6.67 万亿元人民币），接近一年前的八倍。
Meta 的支出承诺同样大幅攀升，未来支出总额超过 8,000 亿美元（现汇率约合 5.34 万亿元人民币）。其中将近一半用于尚未生效的数据中心租约，最长分 30 年支付。Meta CFO 苏珊 · 李在上周的分析师电话会议上说：“我们预计将继续大举投资，支持核心业务和新兴 AI 项目。”
今年商界的一大争论，是科技企业斥资数千亿美元建设 AI 数据中心，究竟能否收回投资。Alphabet 和 Meta 都是全球最赚钱的企业之一，却因投资有望改变行业格局的新业务，出现自由现金流由正转负的情况。
不过，五家公司的支出并非全部用于数据中心，披露口径也不完全一致，因此很难直接比较。
例如，Meta 的部分预算用于 Reality Labs 部门的消费级硬件产品，Alphabet 和亚马逊的计划支出则包括内容授权费用。本次统计也没有计入现有租约和债务等其他大额支出。
五家公司未来的租赁付款承诺合计 1.3 万亿美元（现汇率约合 8.67 万亿元人民币），其他采购承诺合计 1.9 万亿美元（现汇率约合 12.67 万亿元人民币）。除微软外，数据均取自各家公司最新财报。微软的采购和建设订单数据来自截至 6 月底的年度报告，该公司此后尚未更新这两项数据。
甲骨文是首家因投资 AI 数据中心而陷入自由现金流为负的大型科技公司。在本周早些时候举行的投资者说明会上，甲骨文预计到 2028 年恢复正自由现金流，并计划通过供应商融资和客户预付款等方式，减少项目初期需要自行承担的资金支出。
来源：IT之家·人工智能 · ithome.com

report.summary: Bloomberg: Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle have committed over $3 trillion to AI data centers, raising questions about returns and cash-flow pressure.
report.background: The commitments come as generative AI demand pushes hyperscalers to secure land, power, chips, and long-term data-center capacity. Companies disclose purchase and lease obligations in filings, giving a rare view of multiyear spending. The race intensified after ChatGPT and cloud AI services, with Oracle repositioning around AI cloud contracts. Investors are debating whether hundreds of billions in annual capex can earn adequate returns, especially as depreciation, energy costs, and lease obligations rise. Long-term contracts also shift risk across suppliers, landlords, and customers, while power availability and grid connections become bottlenecks. Bloomberg's tally aggregates the five firms' latest disclosures, though accounting scopes differ.
key_points: The five companies’ disclosed commitments exceed $3 trillion: about $1.3 trillion in future lease payments and $1.9 trillion in other purchase obligations. Alphabet alone reports over $1 trillion, nearly eight times a year earlier; Meta exceeds $800 billion, with nearly half tied to data-center leases lasting up to 30 years.

Oracle is the first major tech company to post negative free cash flow because of AI data-center investment. It expects to return to positive free cash flow by 2028 and plans to rely on vendor financing and customer prepayments to reduce upfront capital outlays, a model that shifts financing burden across the supply chain.

The totals are not directly comparable. Meta’s figure includes Reality Labs consumer hardware, while Alphabet and Amazon include content-licensing costs. The tally excludes existing leases and debt, and Microsoft’s purchase and construction orders come from its June annual report, not the latest quarter.

Spending is split between near-term construction and decades-long contracts, creating duration risk. Even highly profitable firms face swings in free cash flow as depreciation and lease payments mount. The core debate is whether AI revenue growth can justify the scale and timing of these commitments.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the commitments entrench a compute arms race: access to power, land, and chips becomes a competitive moat, and smaller players may depend on these clouds or struggle to match scale. Financing innovation—vendor financing, prepayments, and lease structures—will matter as much as model quality. For developers, more capacity should ease GPU shortages over time, but capex recovery may keep inference and storage pricing firm; optimizing workloads and portability will remain valuable. For regular users, AI products should improve and broaden, yet costs may be passed through via subscriptions or usage limits, and provider concentration could shape defaults. The main risk is a supply overbuild if demand growth slows.
report.tools: To follow the buildout, track OpenCost and Kubecost for cloud-cost transparency, MLPerf for infrastructure efficiency benchmarks, Epoch AI for compute-trend data, and Cloud Carbon Footprint for energy and emissions. SemiAnalysis and Bloomberg’s earnings summaries are useful for capex and lease disclosures; IEA data-center energy reports provide grid context.
